assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks transformed precision timekeeping and enable exceptionally sensitive tests and measurements.
assessment.attribution: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and Ye's decisive experimental development form a clear, complementary attribution.
assessment.maturity: Independent clock realizations, steadily improved performance, and broad metrological uptake make this a fully mature achievement.
uncertainties: The eventual scope of applications beyond metrology remains open, although the fundamental experimental advance is unambiguous.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry established a powerful family of quantum measurements with major consequences for inertial sensing and fundamental tests.
assessment.attribution: Bordé supplied foundational interferometric concepts and Kasevich made landmark precision implementations; the wider field complicates any three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been reproduced extensively and have become precision instruments rather than isolated demonstrations.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among foundational atom-interferometry contributors is necessarily incomplete in a limited laureate set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made coherent light-matter physics available in engineered superconducting circuits and opened a major experimental quantum platform.
assessment.attribution: Blais provided central theoretical framing, while Wallraff and Schoelkopf delivered defining experimental demonstrations; Girvin's contribution is also substantial.
assessment.maturity: The platform is deeply replicated and has enabled precision quantum control, measurement, and scalable-device research.
uncertainties: It remains difficult to separate the foundational circuit-QED advance cleanly from the broader superconducting-qubit enterprise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics brought macroscopic motion into the quantum-control regime and created versatile new measurement technology.
assessment.attribution: Cleland, Aspelmeyer, and Kippenberg represent complementary experimental and conceptual advances, though the community has many important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Quantum-limited measurement and control have been demonstrated across several mechanical implementations.
uncertainties: The extent to which macroscopic quantum control has produced a single defining discovery rather than a broad platform is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of NV spins created an exceptionally useful solid-state quantum sensor and spin-photon platform.
assessment.attribution: Jelezko and Wrachtrup were central to single-defect coherent-control experiments, with Lukin important for quantum-sensing and quantum-network development.
assessment.maturity: The techniques are widely reproduced and underpin sensing experiments from nanoscale magnetometry to quantum-device research.
uncertainties: The proposed grouping spans several related advances, and attribution across early optical-detection work requires careful historical review.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser was a genuinely new semiconductor-laser principle with wide practical and scientific impact in the infrared.
assessment.attribution: Faist and Capasso are directly associated with the invention and realization, while Cho's heterostructure technology was enabling and foundational.
assessment.maturity: The technology is robust, broadly deployed, and has opened important spectroscopic and sensing capabilities.
uncertainties: The appropriate balance between the device invention and its prerequisite epitaxial-heterostructure work needs close attribution review.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic band-gap concepts changed how physicists design and control electromagnetic modes in structured materials.
assessment.attribution: John and Yablonovitch supplied seminal independent ideas and demonstrations, while Joannopoulos was central to the theoretical and computational foundations.
assessment.maturity: Photonic-crystal physics is experimentally established and continues to influence integrated optics, emitters, and wave control.
uncertainties: The achievement covers a broad field whose applications have developed unevenly across spectral ranges and platforms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction supplied the essential physical and information-theoretic route from fragile qubits to fault-tolerant computation.
assessment.attribution: Shor, Steane, and Kitaev made distinct foundational contributions to codes, fault tolerance, and topological protection.
assessment.maturity: Core principles have been repeatedly demonstrated, but full-scale fault-tolerant computation is still developing.
uncertainties: The practical threshold for broadly useful fault-tolerant machines has not yet been reached.
The field has an unusually extensive set of foundational contributors beyond three names.
